description.narrative: Asia Pacific Forum for Women Law and Development (APWLD) is a regional membership-based organisation including 268 members from 30 countries across the Asia Pacific Region. The aim of the organisation is 1) To strengthen feminist movements at local, national and regional levels and in particular to support the most marginalised women; 2) To amplify the influence, impact and voice of Asia Pacific women´s rights advocates in local, national, regional and global policy setting bodies; 3) To facilitate the production of evidence-based research and tools for advocacy outcomes and movement building; and 4) To build the capacities of women´s rights organisations and movements in the region using right-base perspectives. The stakeholders to the contribution are APWLD´s 268 member organisations and their communities’ representing women from grassroot level and marginalised groups and women at policy level.

Asia Pacific Forum for Women, Law and Development (APWLD) är en regional medlemsbaserad organisation med 268 medlemmar från 30 länder i Asien och Oceanien. Insatsen syftar till 1) att stärka feministiska rörelser på lokal, nationell och regional nivå med särskilt fokus på de mest marginaliserade kvinnorna; 2) att öka deras påverkansmöjligheter i nationella, regionala och globala fora; 3) att stödja evidensbaserad forskning och kvinnorättsorganisationers uppbyggnad och möjlighet till påverkan; och att 4) bygga upp kapaciteten hos kvinnorättsorganisationer och -rörelser i regionen med hjälp av rättighetsbaserade arbetssätt och perspektiv.

In the Strategic Plan (2022-2026), APWLD ´s overall goal is threefold; to promote women´s human rights in the region; to empower women in the Asia Pacific region to use law as an instrument for change for equality, justice, peace and development; and to strengthen womens rights movements and feminist activism across the Asia Pacific Region.
This will be done by focusing on four overarching objectives for the five year period;
1.To strengthen feminist movements at local, national and regional levels and in particular to support the most marginalised women.
2.To amplify the influence, impact and voice of Asia Pacific women´s rights advocates in local, national, regional and global policy setting bodies.
3. To facilitate the production of evidence-based research and tools for advocacy outcomes and movement building; and
4) To build the capacities of women´s rights organisations and movements in the region using rights-based perspectives and intersection of patriarchy, globalisation, fundamentalisms and militarisation.
According to APWLD's Strategic Plan (2022-2026) four overarching objectives will be integrated through eleven integrated programs. These programs cover comprehensive critical challenges in the region including protection on women human right defenders, climate change, labour and decent work, migration, international trade agreements, feminist legal networks and women political leadership.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
In 2023, APWLD has increased its membership and now include 295 members (27 new members) from 31 countries/territories in the region. In 2023, APWLD secretariat grew and consist of 31 staff members.
Some key highlights from the year 2023 reflects results in APWLDs work:
-17,286 grassroots women and their communities received support from APLWD to build their analysis, political organising and advocacy capacity. During 2023 APWLD produced 148 new feminist knowledge tools and resources, 29 publications and 1,005 multimedia contents.
-APWLD resourced and supported 61 grassroot feminist women´s rights activists to directly engage in 15 high-level advocacy spaces to amplify Asia Pacific womens voices and feminist analysis at the sub-regional, regional and global spaces. In 2023, FPAR, Womanifesto, and FDJ monitoring resulted in formation of 39 new women´s groups at the local level and grassroot level to advance women human rights and development justice.
